title: Local work bound for Fourier estimation
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{\pm1\}$ be a Boolean function, and let $\mathcal F$ be a nonempty finite family of subsets of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$. Let $\varepsilon,\delta\in\mathbb Q$ satisfy $0<\varepsilon,\delta\le 1/2$. For any possible outcome of the confidence-parameter finite-family Fourier estimator, its charged local work $w$, viewed as a rational number, satisfies $w\le 32|\mathcal F|^3(n+1)L/\varepsilon^2$, where $L$ is the failure-bit count associated with confidence parameter $\delta/|\mathcal F|$.
hypotheses_covered: outcome belongs to the support of the estimator's output-and-cost distribution
